name: Six Great Rivers and the Peoples on Their Banks
description: The Ganges, Yangtze, Mekong, Congo, Mississippi and Amazon: the rice, cities, temples and kingdoms they fed, and the traders, empires and dams that came later.

checkpoints.name: Rice and holy water
checkpoints.note: Farmers along the Yangtze grow rice in flooded paddy fields. On the Ganges, Varanasi becomes a holy city, and the Buddha gives his first teaching nearby. The Maurya Empire rules from the Ganges plain, and its emperor Ashoka sends Buddhist teachers far beyond it.

checkpoints.name: Kingdoms on the banks
checkpoints.note: In 208 the Battle of Red Cliffs on the Yangtze stops a northern warlord and helps split China into three kingdoms. The Gupta Empire flourishes on the Ganges plain, and pilgrims gather where rivers meet for an early Kumbh Mela. From 802 the Khmer Empire grows rich on the Mekong basin's rice, ruled from Angkor.

checkpoints.name: Temples and mounds
checkpoints.note: Near the Mississippi, Cahokia grows into the largest town north of Mexico, with great earth mounds. The Khmer build Angkor Wat, but Angkor is largely abandoned after 1431. Shanghai becomes a county town on the Yangtze delta, and the Kingdom of Kongo rises near the mouth of the Congo.

checkpoints.name: Strangers on the water
checkpoints.note: Portuguese ships reach the Congo in the 1480s and Kongo's king becomes a Christian. In 1542 a Spanish party travels the length of the Amazon. The Louisiana Purchase of 1803 gives the United States control of the Mississippi, where Mark Twain works as a steamboat pilot before writing Huckleberry Finn.

checkpoints.name: Rubber, dams and nations
checkpoints.note: In the Congo Free State, forced labour for rubber kills vast numbers of people, and Belgium takes over the Belgian Congo in 1908. The Democratic Republic of the Congo wins independence in 1960, and Patrice Lumumba is killed in 1961. Bangladesh is born on the Ganges delta, the Three Gorges Dam spans the Yangtze, and the Amazon rainforest shrinks.
